The idea

What a DreamBooklet is

DreamBooklet is a personalised keepsake for young children. It takes a child's name and a set of dreams, then turns them into a printed book the child can hold, read, and keep.

The book does not ask a child to choose one job. Each page places the child in a different role and ties it to a value: a doctor who is kind and helpful, an astronaut who is curious and brave, an artist who is creative and joyful.

More than what a child may become, the book speaks to who they already are: curious, kind, and full of wonder.

For a parent, it is a plain way to talk about character with a young child. Kindness, courage, honesty, and effort come up on their own, one page at a time, so a child grows up seeing these as part of who they are.

I listen, I care, I help you heal. With gentle hands and heart that feels.

From Ivanshika's booklet
What's inside

What's in the book

Every booklet follows the same four parts. The names, the dreams, and the words change for each child.

Printed keepsake 20 pages 8.5 x 8.5 inches Soft watercolour throughout
1

A letter to the child

The book opens with a short note to the child by name. It explains, in plain words, that a dream is a happy thought about what they may become.

2

Their name, as qualities

The child's name becomes an acrostic. Each letter stands for a quality, so Ivanshika reads as Important, Valuable, Amazing, and on through her nine letters.

3

Ten dreams, ten values

Ten spreads show the child in a different role. Each role carries a value, written as a short rhyme in the child's own voice.

4

A gentle goodbye

The book closes on a calm note: go forward with honesty, care, and a hopeful heart.

The values

A value behind every dream

This is the heart of the book. The child's name holds a set of qualities, and each dream carries a value. Read together, they give a child a simple language for character, and give a parent something to return to.
